newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso reverses gains on late dollar demand.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso reverses gains on late dollar demand.

text.p: Mexican benchmark 48-hour peso cotracts reversed their earlier firmness to close slightly weaker on Monday due to demand for dollars by foreign brokers hedging against strong forthcoming U.S. inflation data, traders said.
"Dollars were in supply in the market, but foreign dealers stepped in to buy ahead of tomorrow's data,' a trader said, referring to U.S. consumer inflation figures.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 0.2 and 0.3 centavos weaker, respectively, at 7.9180/7.9200 and 7.9120/7.9150 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 3.05 centavos firmer at 7.8950/7.8975 per dollar.

Dealers said they feared yields on U.S. long bonds could rise to 7.25 percent in the coming days if U.S. consumer inflation data were strong. U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds were off 1/32 to yield 7.17 percent in late trade.
"I think foreign brokers went long on dollars rather than just squaring positions," a trader said.
